answers.answer: An Exile who takes Oathkeeper during Act cannot win as Usurper at the next Wake: at that Wake, Usurper/Visionary victory is checked before the Oathkeeper title flips to Usurper. They can first win at the following Wake, if they still hold the title and meet its goal, or at round eight if that endgame arrives first while they are still Usurper. If someone takes the title away, they cannot win as Usurper; taking it back gives them Oathkeeper again and restarts the sequence.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: ‘Victory was checked before this flip’; ‘Losing title prevents this win; retaking resets it to Oathkeeper and restarts the sequence.’

answers.answer: Supremacy matches Conquest; People matches Rebellion; Protection matches Sanctuary; Devotion matches Faith. For any Visionary win, the Exile must have their true Vision revealed and complete its goal at Wake, and all players combined must have drawn at least 3 Visions from the world deck. For Conquest and Sanctuary, ‘most’ means strictly more than every other player, so a tie for most does not qualify. The summary does not state whether ties count for the Rebellion or Faith Vision goals.
answers.evidence: Oathkeeper title and four Oaths table; Visionary victory paragraph states the universal three-draw requirement and strictly-more rule for Conquest/Sanctuary only.

answers.answer: At the ends of rounds 5, 6, and 7, roll the end die only if the Chancellor or a Citizen is Oathkeeper. The game ends on 6 in round 5, 5–6 in round 6, or 3–6 in round 7. An Exile Oathkeeper/Usurper prevents those rolls. Round 8 ends automatically; it does not require an end-die roll.
answers.evidence: Stable regime gives the three roll windows and results and says Exile Oathkeeper/Usurper prevents the roll; War exhaustion says round 8 ends automatically.

answers.answer: At the automatic end of round eight, resolve in order: (1) if Chancellor or Citizen is Oathkeeper, Empire wins (Chancellor unless a qualifying Citizen Successor wins alone); (2) otherwise an Exile Usurper wins; (3) otherwise a qualifying revealed Exile Vision wins, with simultaneous qualifying Visions prioritized Conquest, Rebellion, Sanctuary, Faith; (4) otherwise Empire wins (Chancellor unless a qualifying Citizen Successor wins alone), even if an Exile is only Oathkeeper.
answers.evidence: War exhaustion: ‘Check in this exact priority’ followed by four numbered outcomes; Citizen Successor replaces Chancellor win.

answers.answer: Supremacy Successor: hold more relics plus banners than the Chancellor and every other Citizen. People: hold Darkest Secret. Protection: hold People's Favor. Devotion: hold Grand Scepter. Citizens/Chancellor cannot win by a revealed true Vision or by becoming Usurper.
answers.evidence: Oathkeeper title and four Oaths table; Visionary victory paragraph says Citizens/Chancellor cannot win by true Visions or Usurper.

answers.answer: At Wake, a holder of People's Favor chooses either to put 1 favor from their board onto the banner or return 1 banner favor to the least-full suit bank, choosing among ties. They cannot remove its last favor: if it has 1, they must add a favor if able; if they have none, nothing happens. If the banner is already Mob-side, repeat the choice once. After these choices, check the threshold and flip it to Mob if it has at least 6 favor. If it becomes Mob at this check, that does not trigger another repeat during this Wake.
answers.evidence: Wake: mandatory order, item 1, including last-favor exception, Mob repeat, and final 6+ flip.

answers.answer: Rest order: (1) return favor on denizens/edifices to matching suit banks; (2) return secrets on denizens, edifices, and relics to your board, then flip your facedown board secrets faceup; (3) refresh Exile/Chancellor Supply according to warbands remaining in their personal bank, while a Citizen refreshes to the exact Chancellor marker space, including leftmost; (4) save each remaining unspent Supply by moving the marker one extra space left per unspent Supply, capped at leftmost (7 Supply); (5) optionally use Rest powers, each once and in chosen order. The Exile/Chancellor refresh amounts are the listed bank-count brackets in Rest item 3. Citizen Supply is not calculated by counting purple warbands.
answers.evidence: Rest: mandatory order items 1–5; item 3 gives Citizen exact Chancellor marker rule; item 4 gives saved-Supply rule.

answers.answer: Search chooses either the world deck or the discard pile for the pawn's region, never both. A discard-pile Search costs 2 Supply. A world-deck Search costs 2 Supply at 0 Visions drawn, 3 at 1–2, or 4 at 3–5; Darkest Secret replaces the world-deck cost with 2, subject to other modifiers. Draw up to 3, with fewer only if the source runs out, a world-deck Vision stops the draw, or a modifier reduces it; you cannot stop early voluntarily. From the world deck, draw one at a time; on a Vision, announce that a Vision was drawn, stop immediately, and increase the Visions Drawn track by 1. A Vision drawn from a discard pile does not stop the draw or advance the track.
answers.evidence: Actions: Search—2–4 Supply section; distinguishes world-deck Vision stopping/tracking from discard-pile Vision.

answers.answer: Discard cards facedown atop the next region's discard pile in the cycle Cradle → Provinces → Hinterland → Cradle. For cards in hand/advisers, choose the next region based on your pawn's region; never use the same-region pile. When discarding a card at a site in another region, use the cycle based on that card's region instead. Favor on a discarded card immediately returns to its matching suit bank; secrets on it go to the acting player's board facedown.
answers.evidence: ‘Discard destinations’ paragraph gives regional cycle and remote-site rule; discarded-card resources return favor to bank and secrets to actor's board facedown.

answers.answer: Advisers are limited to 3 total, faceup and facedown together. Before playing over the limit, discard an adviser, subject to locks; if the incoming card changes the limit, apply the new limit before playing it, using the lowest of multiple limits. Facedown advisers have no suit, restriction banner, or power, and any card (including site-only cards and Visions) may be held facedown. Later, a facedown adviser may be played faceup to a legal destination or discarded as a minor action; faceup advisers cannot be discarded at will, only when a rule permits/requires it. A revealed true Vision occupies a separate Exile Revealed Vision space, not an adviser slot; revealing a new true Vision replaces and discards the old revealed Vision. Only an Exile may reveal a true Vision; Chancellor/Citizens may hold true Visions facedown but cannot reveal them.
answers.evidence: Search adviser options; Discard destinations adviser retention table; True Vision paragraph; Minor actions.

answers.answer: Muster costs 1 Supply: at your pawn's site, place 1 favor on an empty denizen or intact edifice (no favor or secrets already) and take 2 warbands from your personal bank onto your board; a Citizen takes purple. The card need not be ruled, but a remote ruled site is not eligible; relics and ruins are ineligible. At River, Muster gains one additional warband if you rule it. Trade costs 1 Supply and uses an empty denizen/intact edifice at your pawn's site (not a relic or ruin). Option A: place 1 secret on the card and gain 1 favor plus 1 per matching faceup adviser from the card's suit bank. Option B: place 2 favor on the card and gain 1 shared-bank secret per matching faceup adviser; with no matching advisers, gain zero secrets. Facedown advisers do not match. Finite favor/warband supplies limit gains to available pieces; secrets are unlimited. Costs remain payable even if the gain is reduced to zero.
answers.evidence: Muster and Trade sections plus River site power; Trade expressly states zero secrets with no matching advisers and that costs remain payable.

answers.answer: Recover costs 1 Supply plus the target cost. A facedown relic must be at your site; pay its printed site cost (3 favor to the indicated bank, burn 2 favor, burn 1 secret, or burn 2 secrets), then put it faceup in your personal bank. A banner may be recovered from anywhere, including yourself or the shared bank, by strictly outbidding its current amount: pay more favor than People's Favor holds, or more secrets than Darkest Secret holds. For People's Favor, put the new payment on the banner, then distribute the old favor one at a time to suit banks, starting at any bank and moving in printed order toward the world deck, wrapping as needed; it does not go back to the previous holder, and flip it to normal side if Mob. There is no seizure penalty for Recover. For Darkest Secret, put the new secrets on it; its new holder takes 1 old secret and the previous holder takes the rest. Recovering it from yourself returns all old secrets to yourself; from the shared bank, the remainder stays in the bank. Held/player relics and Reliquary relics cannot be recovered. The summary does not specify a destination for People's Favor's old tokens beyond the suit banks, or a recipient for old Darkest Secret tokens when the prior holder is the shared bank beyond saying the remainder stays there.
answers.evidence: Recover section gives Supply, relic and banner costs, destinations, Mob reversal and Darkest Secret old-secret split.

answers.answer: To recover another player's Darkest Secret, there must be at least one suited card at that player's pawn site whose suit matches none of their faceup advisers. One such mismatching card is enough even if other cards match. A site with no cards or only a ruin protects the banner, because ruins have no suit; facedown advisers also have no suit. If the holder has no faceup advisers, any suited card at their site is unmatched and the banner is recoverable. This protection does not apply when recovering from yourself or the shared bank.
answers.evidence: ‘Darkest Secret protection, corrected by official errata’ paragraph explicitly covers a mismatching card, empty/ruin-only site, and no faceup advisers.

answers.answer: Choose as defender any other player who rules your site or whose pawn is there; if no player rules your site, you may choose bandits. At least one target must be at your pawn's site, and if the defender rules that site you must target it. You may add any of the defender's sites anywhere on the map as targets, with 1 defense die per targeted site. If the defender's pawn is at your site, you may instead/additionally target any of their relics (their printed defense dice), banners (dice equal to resources on the banner), or their pawn and board favor together (2 dice). A co-located defender relic by itself satisfies the local-target requirement. Thus a relic at your site can be targeted even if it is not itself a site; the summary says relic targets are available when the defender's pawn is at your site.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 1–2: defender eligibility, mandatory/local and remote site targets, co-located relic/banner/pawn-favor targets and dice.

answers.answer: Attacker chooses up to as many attack dice as warbands in the attacking force, then applies relevant modifiers and the Oathkeeper (+1 defense die) or Usurper (+2 defense dice) bonus. Defense is shields rolled (double-symbols multiply shields only, with multipliers stacking) plus all defending warbands at targeted sites, plus defender board force if their pawn is at the attacker's site or any target; bandits add 1 per targeted bandit site. Each attack skull immediately kills 1 of the attacker's own force warbands. Count full swords; each pair of hollow swords adds 1, and a leftover hollow sword adds zero. An attacker may sacrifice surviving own force warbands for +1 attack each, but if sacrificing must sacrifice exactly enough to win, never extra. Attack must strictly exceed defense; a tie or lower is a defender win. A missing attack die removed from an empty pool by a plan instead adds a defense die.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 2–5 detail dice, bonuses, defense calculation, skulls, hollow swords, exact sacrifices, and strict win condition.

answers.answer: On attacker victory, first resolve the defender's defeat casualties: the defender kills half the warbands in its defending force, rounded down, returning the rest to board. With Imperial defenders, the Chancellor chooses which defending Imperial warbands die; surviving site warbands go to the Chancellor's board, while surviving warbands already on Citizens' boards stay on those boards. Resolve defeated battle-plan effects immediately after these casualties. Then the attacker may place any number, including zero, of surviving force warbands on any targeted sites; placing zero leaves a site to bandits unless a power applies. The attacker takes all targeted relics and banners. For each banner seized by a means other than Recover, burn 2 resources from it down to a minimum of 1; People's Favor flips to Mob. If pawn and favor were targeted, the attacker may force the defender to travel to a legal chosen site for no Supply, and independently may burn half the defender's board favor, rounded down. Respect travel restrictions; if Shrouded Wood applies, its enemy ruler chooses the destination (Chancellor chooses for the Empire), overriding attacker choice. Next resolve the attacker's victorious battle-plan effects. For either winner, then discard plans from either side that say ‘At end, discard.’ Transfer Supremacy title at the end of the Campaign, not during temporary loss of site rule. The summary does not spell out the destination/state of bandits when an attacker places zero garrisons beyond saying the site is left to bandits.
answers.evidence: Campaign steps 6–8 give defeat-before-target ordering, target effects, victory-plan timing, end-discard cleanup and Supremacy title timing.

answers.answer: If an Imperial player defends, the Chancellor automatically joins as Ally. Other non-attacking Citizens may join with the defender's permission if their pawn is at the attacker's site or a target. Defender and Allies activate modifiers they rule and share defense-side powers as one side; their board warbands add defense only if their pawn is at the attacker's site or a target. They may use plans at Imperial sites and their own advisers, not other players' advisers; a shared plan can be used only once total, by one user who pays its cost. The declared defender chooses order/timing/priority when Allies conflict, including which user takes a shared plan and whether a restrictive plan is declared first. Chancellor chooses which defending Imperial warbands die; surviving site warbands go to Chancellor's board, and surviving Citizen-board warbands stay there. In a Campaign where a Citizen attacks Chancellor or another Citizen, that attacker is non-Imperial for that Campaign; when Chancellor attacks a Citizen, that Citizen is non-Imperial for that Campaign. An intra-Empire Campaign does not make all Citizens non-Imperial.
answers.evidence: Campaign defender step 1 and Imperial defense bullets cover temporary non-Imperial status, allies, shared powers/plans and casualty handling.

answers.answer: Base Travel Supply costs by origin region to destination region: from Cradle, Cradle 1, Provinces 2, Hinterland 4; from Provinces, each region 2; from Hinterland, Cradle 4, Provinces 2, Hinterland 3. Travel is to any different site, not only adjacent. Reveal a facedown destination and place its printed favor/secrets from the shared bank and its printed number of relics facedown from the relic deck. Apply fixed-number cost first, then other increases/decreases. Any applicable ‘spend no Supply’ free-Travel power is the final override and makes the Supply payment zero despite increases; entry restrictions still apply unless the power ignores them. The summary does not define any additional general timing or destination exceptions beyond the specific site powers it lists.
answers.evidence: Travel matrix and paragraph state facedown-site reveal stocking, fixed cost order, free-Travel override, and site restrictions.

answers.answer: In play, the Grand Scepter holder cannot use its powers the turn they took it, and cannot make an offer on that same turn. On a later turn the holder may offer Citizenship to any Exile, including themself, promising exactly one Reliquary relic; they may also negotiate binding exchanges of favor, secrets, banners, and non-Reliquary relics, and may let the recipient peek at Reliquary relics. Recipient accepts by flipping to Citizen and replacing all their own board/map warbands with purple (if purple is short, recipient chooses which to remove/replace), discarding revealed Vision, flipping Usurper to Oathkeeper, ending their Act if it is their turn, and refreshing to full leftmost Supply. The promised pieces are exchanged, and Chancellor gains the newly uncovered mandatory Reliquary modifier. Forced Citizenship powers use the status-conversion steps but require no negotiated offer or Reliquary gift, and no promised exchange is invented; only actual removal of a Reliquary relic uncovers its modifier. Reliquary relics cannot be traded through other binding-deal powers. The Scepter holder may also exile another Citizen under the separately specified favor payment; self-exile has its own payment and restrictions, rather than being acceptance of an offer.
answers.evidence: Citizenship and exile during play: Grand Scepter, Offer, Acceptance, forced Citizenship and exile subsections.

answers.answer: Chronicle Oath: if the winner won by a Vision alone, the next Oath matches that Vision; otherwise (including multiple victory methods) choose any Oath except the current one. If the winner is an Exile, flip all Citizen boards, including boxed boards, to Exile, then the winner may offer free Chronicle Citizenship to other Exiles except those just flipped; no Scepter, relic gift, or resource payment is needed. An accepting Exile flips their board to Citizen and replaces every garrison at each site they rule with exactly one winner-color warband. Rebuild the world deck by shuffling all denizens remaining in play (excluding cards retained at sites, in Archive, or Dispossessed), then place 10 denizens plus 2 random Visions in the 12-card top stack, 15 denizens plus the remaining 3 Visions in the 18-card next stack, and remaining denizens below. It is 12 cards, not 14, because the Chronicle aid's printed ‘12 denizens + 2’ is erroneous; the correct allocation is 10+2.
answers.evidence: Writing the Chronicle steps 1–2 and step 9 explicitly state Oath choice, Citizenship turnover, and correct 10+2 top stack / aid error.
